question: Can one TuneJS-owned binaural renderer — nearest-position HRIR convolution with linear crossfade — run identically in the offline renderer, a browser AudioWorklet, and a React Native worklet node, under the sustained reference workload?

sources.artifacts/binaural/browser-results.json: fixture v8 offline run, headless Chromium 152: all rows pass including the six dsp-binaural-* kinds at 44100 and 48000 against the direct-convolution reference (synthetic HRTF table)
dsp-live-probes v2, headless Chromium live AudioContext: all five probes pass; dsp-binaural-live recovers the right-ear near tap q16(0.9) at +4 frames and left-ear far tap q16(0.1) at +28 frames per period
sources.artifacts/binaural/native-live-ios.json: full example-app payload, iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 26.5, Release: dsp-live-probes v2 all pass, dsp-binaural-live valueError 0; raw host-node fixture rows still fail as documented (host fan-out/offline-summation limits, unchanged)
sources.artifacts/binaural/native-live-android.j: same payload, Android API 35 arm64 emulator: dsp-live-probes v2 all pass, dsp-binaural-live valueError 0; raw host-node rows fail identically
sources.artifacts/binaural/workload-binaural-600: reference workload, binaural mode, 600 s headless Chromium 152: status pass — 1201 scheduled / 0 late / 0 skipped transport events, 34505 pose updates at 60 Hz, 10139 meter reads with 0 dropped frames, peakVoices 12, clockDrift 0.020 s over 600 s
sources.artifacts/binaural/workload-stereo-60.js: 60 s stereo control run: pass, 0 late events, 0 dropped meter frames — no stereo regression
sources.artifacts/binaural/ios-worklets-launch-c: one react-native-worklets launch crash (createWorkletRuntime SIGSEGV) during the iOS run — the known intermittent host crash; relaunch succeeded

asset.grid: 794 positions — elevations -90..90 step 15, azimuths 0..355 step 5, single position per pole; selected from the dense 9201-file SADIE II D1 grid with zero angular error (every target name exists exactly)
asset.tables: 256 taps, int16, rates 44100 and 48000; verified byte-exact against the source WAVs within int16 quantization (max 1.5e-5)
asset.identity: SADIE II v2-2, subject D1, Neumann KU100, Apache-2.0; azimuth converted (360 - sadieAz) mod 360 to clockwise-from-front

kernel.module: src/dsp.ts — ConvolverInput (shared input-side FDL) + PartitionedConvolver slots with setKernel; BinauralEffect: mono = mean(inputs) * a-rate gain, nearest-HRTF pair per block, linear crossfade w=(i+1)/N over smoothingFrames, both ears fed identical x
kernel.agreement: BinauralEffect matches binauralReference to <= 1e-9 on all six programs at both rates (unit); bundled tunejs-binaural worklet processor matches <= 1e-5 (Float32 boundary); native worklet simulation likewise
kernel.fix during integration: refactor introduced a tail-partition MAC typo (x.re vs x.im) breaking kernels > 2048 taps; caught by the convolve() parity test, corrected before merge

conclusions: spatialSource({rendering:'binaural', hrtf}) is supported on the browser adapter and on the native adapter's TuneJS DSP path; it requires adapter.dsp and an explicit hrtf asset and never falls back to stereo
binaural output is deterministic and shared across live and offline paths: the same kernel class serves Engine.render, the AudioWorklet, and the RN worklet
the binaural workload sustains the reference load within all existing thresholds; no new counters were added, so audible-dropout freedom is still not concluded (same caveat as stereo)
native raw-host fixtures (strict timing, fan-out, offline summation) remain failing by design — the TuneJS DSP path is what carries binaural natively
the intermittent react-native-worklets launch crash re-occurred once on iOS; it remains a host reliability issue for the device gates, not a correctness blocker
stillOpen: Firefox/Safari and Android Chrome binaural fixtures
